text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment of this newborn's yellowish skin discoloration, could you please tell me the infant's age in hours and when you first noticed the jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant been feeding well, and have you noticed any signs of lethargy, poor suck, or high-pitched crying? REQUEST TEST: Total_and_Direct_Bilirubin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 7 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.6 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin levels are mildly elevated and predominantly unconjugated, which is common in breastfed infants at this age. Given the normal feeding history and lack of concerning neurological signs, this appears to be physiological jaundice. I will monitor the infant closely, but no immediate intervention is required.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of jaundice from face to trunk with scleral icterus and mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a well-appearing, fully breastfed 5-day-old is classic for physiological jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological jaundice
